Synopsis:
Researchers from the University of Cape Town have built a nature-based, off-grid water filtration system in the informal settlement of Langrug, treating 36,000 litres of sewage-polluted river water daily using stones, biochar and sand. Operational since 2018, the system now removes ~99% of toxins, enabling water reuse for community food gardens. The project is positioned as a replicable model for food security under climate-driven water scarcity, particularly relevant to a region already hit by severe drought in 2018.
